newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac calls French election for May 25, June 1.
newsitem.headline: Chirac calls French election for May 25, June 1.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac announced on Monday he was dissolving the National Assembly and called an early parliamentary election for May 25 and June 1.

In a televised address, Chirac said he had decided to bring forward the poll by more than nine months so that the French people could "express themselves clearly on the scale and speed of change over the next five years".

Chirac said France needed a far-reaching reform of the state to make possible a cut in public spending, which was the only way to reduce taxes and welfare charges which weighed too heavily on citizens and discouraged initiative.
"To succeed, France needs a new impetus," the president said.

He said an early vote was also vital to prepare for major decisions on European integration, especially the switch to a single currency which he said was "essential if we want to assert ourselves as a great economic and political power", with the euro on an equal footing with the dollar and the yen.

"To approach these deadlines from a position of strength, to build a Europe that respects the genius of its member nations and is capable of rivalling the great world blocs, your agreement and support are essential," Chirac said.
